comparisons.peer_summary: The company uses tangible equity (shareholders' equity reduced by goodwill and intangibles, excluding MSRs) to evaluate equity usage and growth, defining specific ratios for return on average tangible equity, tangible equity ratio, and tangible book value per share.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America disclose Tangible Book Value Per Share (TBVPS) as a key non-GAAP financial metric to evaluate capital and equity usage. JPM explicitly states its TBVPS grew 13.0% to $97.30, while Bank of America defines TBVPS as adjusted common shareholders' equity divided by common shares outstanding and notes it is a key measure for evaluating business performance alongside return on tangible equity.

sentences.text: ● Tangible book value per common share represents adjusted ending common shareholders' equity divided by ending common shares outstanding.

comparisons.peer_summary: Return on Tangible Common Equity (RoTCE) and Tangible Book Value Per Share (TBVPS) are identified as non-GAAP financial measures, with detailed information referenced in the Capital Resources section.
comparisons.comparison: Citigroup identifies TBVPS as a non-GAAP financial measure, aligning with JPMorgan's treatment of the metric. While JPM reports specific growth and ending values for TBVPS, Citigroup's disclosure serves as a definitional reference pointing readers to the 'Capital Resources' section for detailed TBVPS calculations, confirming both firms treat this as a distinct, non-GAAP capital adequacy metric.

comparisons.peer_topic: Book value per common share calculation
comparisons.peer_summary: Book value and tangible book value per common share are based on basic shares (common shares outstanding and certain restricted stock units) totaling 322.9 million as of December 2024 and 337.1 million as of December 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs calculates Tangible Book Value Per Common Share as tangible common shareholders' equity divided by basic shares, similar to JPMorgan's definition. Both firms use this metric to assess capital adequacy; however, Goldman Sachs highlights the reduction in basic share count from 337.1 million in 2023 to 322.9 million in 2024, whereas JPMorgan highlights the percentage growth rate of the metric itself.

sentences.text: • Book value per common share and tangible book value per common share are based on common shares outstanding and restricted stock units granted to employees with no future service requirements and not subject to performance or market conditions (collectively, basic shares) of 322.9 million as of December 2024 and 337.1 million as of December 2023. We believe that tangible book value per common share (tangible common shareholders' equity divided by basic shares) is meaningful because it is a measure that we and investors use to assess capital adequacy. Tangible book value per common share is a non-GAAP measure and may not be comparable to similar non-GAAP measures used by other companies.
